purpose: Researcher review, not completed human scores

case.task: Describe the sound that comes from your grandfather’s shop each evening.
case.student_text: The bell ring at six every evening, and we can hear it from our kitchen. The bells near the shop arent very loud, but they remind my grandfather to close his shop.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: The bell rings at six every evening, and we can hear it from our kitchen. The bells near the shop aren't very loud, but they remind my grandfather to close his shop.
acceptable_alternatives: The bell rings at six every evening, and we can hear it from our kitchen. The bells near the shop are not very loud, but they remind my grandfather to close his shop.

errors.explanation: Add -s to the verb with the singular subject bell.
Write are not as the contraction aren't.

case.task: Tell a new barber how you choose a haircut.
case.student_text: Marta trim my hair at the small salon near the park every month. She asks me to choose a picture from a book, then checks the length in the mirror. I like the blue chairs there.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: Marta trims my hair at the small salon near the park every month. She asks me to choose a picture from a book, then checks the length in the mirror. I like the blue chairs there.

errors.explanation: Add -s to the verb with the singular subject Marta.

case.task: Write about when your family puts up a calendar.
case.student_text: We put a new calendar on the kitchen door at October. My brother marks his birthday with a green pen, and I circle the days when our cousins come to stay.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: We put a new calendar on the kitchen door in October. My brother marks his birthday with a green pen, and I circle the days when our cousins come to stay.
acceptable_alternatives: We put a new calendar on the kitchen door during October. My brother marks his birthday with a green pen, and I circle the days when our cousins come to stay.

errors.explanation: Use in with a month.

case.task: Describe the furniture in a quiet corner.
case.student_text: There are two furniture beside the reading lamp: a low table and a small chair. I sit there to draw after dinner, and my cat sleeps on the rug nearby.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: There are two pieces of furniture beside the reading lamp: a low table and a small chair. I sit there to draw after dinner, and my cat sleeps on the rug nearby.
acceptable_alternatives: There are two items of furniture beside the reading lamp: a low table and a small chair. I sit there to draw after dinner, and my cat sleeps on the rug nearby.

errors.explanation: Furniture is uncountable; use pieces of furniture to count separate items.

case.task: Compare two paths to a playground.
case.student_text: The path beside the pond is longer that the path near the houses. I use the short path when I am late, but I walk beside the water when I have more time.

gold.corrected_text: The path beside the pond is longer than the path near the houses. I use the short path when I am late, but I walk beside the water when I have more time.

errors.explanation: Use than after a comparative adjective.

case.task: Describe a lighthouse that visitors can see at night.
case.student_text: The lighthouse flash twice every night when the sea is dark. Its white beam moves across the rocks, and a small sign says the path is closed becaus the tide is high.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: The lighthouse flashes twice every night when the sea is dark. Its white beam moves across the rocks, and a small sign says the path is closed because the tide is high.

errors.explanation: Add -es to flash with the singular subject lighthouse.
The correct spelling is because.

case.task: Write two sentences comparing an old doorway with a new one.

gold.corrected_text: The new door is as wide as the old one, but its colour is much lighter. My uncle painted both doors last week and left the brushes outside to dry.

errors.explanation: Use the base adjective between as and as.

case.task: Tell a friend about a hobby you enjoy.
case.student_text: I enjoy to draw small pictures when I have free time. I usually sit by the kitchen window and sketch flowers or cups. My cousin likes painting, so sometimes we work at the table together.

gold.corrected_text: I enjoy drawing small pictures when I have free time. I usually sit by the kitchen window and sketch flowers or cups. My cousin likes painting, so sometimes we work at the table together.

case.task: Ask a friend when they leave and describe the journey.
case.student_text: What time you leave for the airport tomorrow? I can drive you there if you need a ride. The trip dont take long early in the morning, and we can stop for coffee before your flight.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: What time do you leave for the airport tomorrow? I can drive you there if you need a ride. The trip doesn't take long early in the morning, and we can stop for coffee before your flight.

errors.explanation: Use do before the subject in a present simple question.
Use doesn't with the singular subject trip.

case.task: Describe where you keep your clothes.
case.student_text: I keep my coats and scarves on the bedroom, beside the door. A small basket holds my gloves, and my shoes stay under the bed. This makes it easy to get ready when I leave home early.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: I keep my coats and scarves in the bedroom, beside the door. A small basket holds my gloves, and my shoes stay under the bed. This makes it easy to get ready when I leave home early.

errors.explanation: Use in for something located inside a room.

case.task: Tell a friend about information you found for a class project.
case.student_text: I found many information about the town library for my project. The website also showed a useful map and two opening times for the weekend. I copied a details into my notebook so I can share it with my group.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: I found a lot of information about the town library for my project. The website also showed a useful map and two opening times for the weekend. I copied a detail into my notebook so I can share it with my group.
acceptable_alternatives: I found much information about the town library for my project. The website also showed a useful map and two opening times for the weekend. I copied a detail into my notebook so I can share it with my group.

errors.explanation: Information is uncountable; use a lot of information rather than many information.
Use a singular noun after a.

case.task: Describe a regular family visit.
case.student_text: We visit my aunt at Sunday afternoons, usually after lunch. She lives above a small bakery, so we can walk there in ten minutes. She has a collection of postcards from different towns, and she shows us one each time we visit.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: We visit my aunt on Sunday afternoons, usually after lunch. She lives above a small bakery, so we can walk there in ten minutes. She has a collection of postcards from different towns, and she shows us one each time we visit.

errors.explanation: Use on with a day of the week.

case.task: Describe what people are doing before a game.
case.student_text: The team members are wait in the school gym for their captain. One student is filling a bottle, and two friends talking about the score. Their coach is checking a list on the wall before practice.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: The team members are waiting in the school gym for their captain. One student is filling a bottle, and two friends are talking about the score. Their coach is checking a list on the wall before practice.

errors.explanation: Use waiting after are to form the present continuous.
Add are before talking to form the present continuous for the action happening now.

case.task: Write about two people in a family photograph.
case.student_text: In this old photograph, her is my grandmother beside the fireplace. She is holding a cat, and my grandfather is sitting next to her. Them are my great-aunts, who came to visit us one summer.
case.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: In this old photograph, she is my grandmother beside the fireplace. She is holding a cat, and my grandfather is sitting next to her. They are my great-aunts, who came to visit us one summer.

errors.explanation: Use the subject pronoun she before is; the longer fragment identifies this occurrence.
Use the subject pronoun they as the subject of are.
